sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: AI Video Synthesis and Virtual Avatar Generation Software

stage_1.expense_line_item: Minimum endowment declaration (USD 10,000 equivalent) and notarial attestation (non-disbursed at incorporation; capitalized as foundation assets)
stage_1.charging_authority: Not applicable — internal capital declaration under Ley 25/1995
stage_1.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital for Private Interest Foundations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley 22 de 2016; applicable registry provisions in Título II, Registro Público de Panamá regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Registro Público de Panamá (RPP)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución / Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarized Foundation Charter registered with the Public Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial capital of USD 10,000 (or equivalent in another currency) must be stated in the Foundation Charter; the capital may be paid in installments or in kind, no escrow account is required, and no deposit proof is required at registration, but the subscribed patrimony must be identified and accepted by the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Founder subscribes and contributes the initial capital of USD 10,000 to the Foundation patrimony, held by the Foundation Council, in cash or kind. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [Panama City address] and the Resident Agent is appointed as required by Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Foundation Council is appointed: Chairperson [Name], Secretary [Name], and Treasurer [Name], with full powers to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and manage operations of the AI video synthesis business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina de Certificado de No Objeción
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request online or at the Public Registry counter to obtain a Certificate of No Objection for the proposed foundation name, e.g., 'AvatarGen Panama Private Interest Foundation'. The name must include 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or an acceptable abbreviation, and must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered entity.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Copy of the settlor/founder identification document
Simplified power of attorney if a law firm files on behalf of the founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the same office or immediately submit a new name reservation request; a clean certificate is typically issued within 2 business days after the objection is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Foundation Charter before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The settlor and the initial Foundation Council members appear before a Panamanian notary and execute the Foundation Charter as a public deed. The deed must state the foundation name, registered office, initial capital, purpose, beneficiary rules, and the name of the Resident Agent. All pages must be notarized and the settlor must declare that the foundation has a lawful purpose.
required_dossiers: Certificate of No Objection from the Public Registry
Foundation Charter draft prepared by a Panamanian attorney
Passport or valid identification of the settlor and initial council members
Statement of registered office address in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a legal deficiency, the parties execute an amendment deed or addendum to the Charter and re-sign; corrected pages are re-notarized immediately at the same notary office without a new court proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter with the Public Registry for registration under Law 25 of 1995. The Registry will verify the name, capital clauses, and legal formalities, then issue an official inscription number and stamped copies.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
Notary certification of due execution
Certificate of No Objection for the foundation name
Copy of the settlor's identification and, if applicable, the Resident Agent's acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect or query, the attorney files a written response and any required correction within ten business days; after curing the observation, the Registry proceeds with the inscription. Expedited processing may be obtained by paying an urgent filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration – RUC Enrollment with DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Public Registry inscription, apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) at the DGI portal or local branch. Submit the registered Charter and identification of the foundation's legal representative. The taxpayer file will record the foundation as the entity for income tax and invoicing purposes under the territorial taxation system.
required_dossiers: Registered Foundation Charter (stamped by the Public Registry)
RUC application form (Formulario único de registro)
Copy of the legal representative's passport or cedula
Proof of registered office address
Notarized acceptance of the Resident Agent or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is queried for inconsistent business address or agent data, correct the registration details online and resubmit electronic scans within three business days; any late fee is waived if the error was administrative and corrected within the same week.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales / Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a municipal license application for the commercial activity of 'AI software development and digital video generation services' under ISIC 6201. The Municipality will issue an Aviso de Operación covering the Panamanian registered office, which is sufficient for a SaaS business with no physical manufacturing component. The annual municipal fee is calculated on the declared taxable revenue.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate issued by DGI
Registered Foundation Charter
Municipal license application form
Identification of the legal representative
Proof of registered office lease or ownership title
Initial declaration of estimated annual revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality rejects or queries the application, the foundation may file a written objection together with revised revenue projections and lease documentation; payment of the maximum provisional fee secures an interim Aviso de Operación while the tax classification is resolved.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales; no industrial manufacturing licensing authority applies to pure AI SaaS operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) under the Panamanian Municipal Tax Code

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Non-industrial digital service; no Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) category required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; software-only operations produce no wastewater or VOC emissions, and any physical server-hosting environmental obligations are borne by the cloud infrastructure provider under its own EIA compliance regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No specialized fire safety certificate is required for a pure virtual-office software operation. If a physical floor is leased in Panama, the workplace must obtain a basic occupancy certificate from the building owner, electrical and fire extinguisher inspections by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, and a general workplace safety affidavit. The National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC) approval is not triggered for a low-risk AI development office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (General Directorate of Revenue) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online filing and registration portal: e-Tax / SIME at https://etax.mef.gob.pa; institutional portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must engage a licensed Panamanian attorney as resident agent; register the foundation deed and obtain legal personality (Personería Jurídica) at the Registro Público de Panamá; then file RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) registration with the DGI through the e-Tax portal using the foundation's constituted documents, domicile agent appointment, and a notarized and apostilled power of attorney; after RUC issuance, the foundation must apply for digital signature (Firma Electrónica) and separately register for ITBMS and electronic invoicing before carrying on taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: The PIF is not a pass-through entity; it is a separate legal person taxed at entity level only on Panama-source income. Foreign-source income, gains, and activities taking place outside Panama fall outside the territorial tax net and are fully excluded from Panamanian income tax. The PIF remains subject to fixed annual franchise/annuity fees and to ITBMS only on Panama-situs taxable supplies; active AI SaaS operations are taxable in Panama only if the underlying service is rendered, used, or exploited within Panamanian territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections include: (1) registration as an ordinary ITBMS taxpayer versus a simplified small-taxpayer regime where turnover thresholds are met; (2) election to file income tax returns on a calendar-year basis with standard DGI forms; (3) election to register as an exporter for zero-rating and input-VAT refund purposes; and (4) alignment with OECD hybrid-mismatch outcomes through Panama's territorial rules and treaty tie-breaker provisions, though no standalone hybrid-election statute exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 50,000 (USD 50,000) in annual gross turnover for mandatory general ITBMS registration in Balboa (pegged 1:1 to USD); however, foreign and domestic suppliers of digital services, including AI avatar video SaaS, must register for ITBMS regardless of turnover, and non-resident digital platforms are required to collect ITBMS on supplies to Panamanian recipients.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) is in force for all RUC taxpayers through the DGI e-Tax/SIME platform. Invoices must be issued through DGI-approved software, transmitted to the DGI for prior validation and authorization via web services/API, include a QR code and digital stamp, and bear the taxpayer's electronic signature. Large taxpayers are subject to stricter real-time clearance requirements; non-resident digital service providers must issue simplified compliant records and submit periodic ITBMS returns electronically.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated at 0% ITBMS under the Panamanian ITBMS statute. AI avatar video generation and AIGC SaaS services qualify as exported services when supplied to non-resident customers, paid from abroad, and effectively used or consumed entirely outside Panama. Eligibility requires: ITBMS registration and exporter status, a written contract or license agreement with the non-resident counterparty, verifiable payment inflow through banking or licensed payment intermediaries (Stripe/Paddle), and supporting records demonstrating the foreign situs of delivery and use; related input ITBMS credits are then claimable as refunds through the DGI export-refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) for physical goods; not applicable to pure SaaS/avatar video exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical shipments; for SaaS: signed license or service contract with the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or bank statements evidencing settlement of export proceeds from abroad
Commercial invoices issued under the DGI electronic-invoicing regime referencing the zero-rated export supply
Stripe/Paddle payment-rail transaction reports and payout statements evidencing non-resident counterparties and foreign-source receipts
Non-resident status evidence (foreign registry extract, tax residency certificate, or jurisdiction of incorporation) for each material customer
ITBMS export declaration and refund application submitted through the DGI e-Tax/SIME portal
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and claw back ITBMS credits where export substantiation is deficient, payment is not repatriated within the substantiation period, or documentation is fraudulent; such adjustments attract recargo interest on underpaid tax, fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the omitted or overclaimed tax, and potential criminal tax-fraud prosecution for knowingly false export records or forged invoices under Panama's tax and criminal statutes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a traditional central bank or a monetary authority with discretionary FX powers. The banking system is supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, 'SBP'), which is the competent prudential and conduct authority for all licensed banks and financial institutions pursuant to Decree Law 9 of 1998. Fiscal agency functions are undertaken by the Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama), which acts as fiscal agent of the State, while the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) governs macroeconomic and financial policy. AML/CFT oversight is exercised by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Law 23 of 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama applies a full, unregulated dollarized monetary framework: the official unit of account is the Balboa (PAB), pegged at 1:1 to the United States dollar, and U.S. dollars circulate as unrestricted legal tender. There is no exchange control board, no prior authorization regime for capital movements, and no restriction on current-account transactions such as software licensing royalties, SaaS subscription fees, or trade payments. Capital-account operations, including shareholder/founder capital injections, loans from non-residents, and distribution of endowments, are fully convertible and may be freely remitted through the domestic banking system. Profit and capital remittance hurdles for a Private Interest Foundation are effectively nil, subject only to standard AML/KYC verification and the Panamanian territorial income tax rules, under which foreign-source income and capital gains earned entirely outside Panama are not subject to Panamanian income tax (Ley 25 de 1995 and Fiscal Code Art. 694).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender, forced conversion, or minimum repatriation timelines applicable in Panama. A Panama Private Interest Foundation engaged in AI video synthesis and SaaS licensing may hold 100% of its export proceeds in USD, EUR, GBP, or any freely convertible currency in any licensed bank without mandatory conversion to PAB. Exporters and service providers must simply comply with standard commercial invoicing, tax record-keeping, and UAF reporting thresholds: cash transactions at or above USD 10,000 and all suspicious transactions must be reported to the UAF under Law 23 of 2015. No percentage of export or licensing proceeds must be surrendered to any state authority.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account; segregated Capital Escrow Account for foundation endowment
Operational USD current account and collections settlement account
Operational USD Account for SaaS collections and disbursements
Capital Escrow Account and operational account for international wire flows
Operational USD Account; boutique international banking and private client services
Operational USD Account with integrated merchant services
Operational USD Account; requires a demonstrable Panamanian nexus and stronger documentary substance
Operational USD Account; retail-oriented, generally unsuitable for non-resident PIF treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium viability as a full treasury rail. Panama does not yet have a dedicated E-Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime equivalent to the EU/UK EMI framework; non-bank fintechs must generally partner with an SBP-licensed bank to hold funds, and the SBP does not directly license standalone digital wallets for corporate multi-currency settlement. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Airwallex, or Payoneer may accept a Panama PIF where the UBO register is transparent, apostilled foundation documents are provided, and the account is used purely for settlement of Stripe/Paddle payouts, but these providers frequently decline private interest foundations due to perceived asset-protection structures, and their funds are not covered by Panamanian deposit insurance. The foundation should therefore treat offshore EMIs as collection-only and daily-sweep balances to a Tier 1 Panamanian bank; for large AI-compute and corporate disbursements, a full SBP-licensed bank account is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under SBP due-diligence rules implementing Law 23 of 2015 and FATF standards, banks must identify the natural person controlling the legal entity, meaning the founder (or, where the founder is itself a body corporate, its senior officer) must normally undergo an in-person or live video interview. In practice, Banco General, Banistmo, Multibank, and Global Bank require the initial visit to be conducted physically by the founder at a Panamanian branch, or alternatively allow a live-video interview where the founder grants a notarized and apostilled power of attorney to the resident Panamanian law firm and provides a certified copy of the foundation deed. Additional foundation council members, protectors, and beneficiaries may usually be onboarded remotely with certified passport copies, professional banking references, and criminal-record certificates issued within the last 90 days. Banks are typically unwilling to open a fully remote account solely on scanned documents without any local intermediary because of correspondent-bank de-risking pressure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived mismatch between PIF legal form and the claimed operating software business: the PIF appears to be a wealth-protection or asset-planning vehicle rather than a genuine AI video synthesis company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the foundation charter (Escritura Pública) clearly expanding the 'objeto' or purpose clause to include software development, IP licensing, AI avatar generation, and SaaS services; deliver an updated Certificado de Personería Jurídica from the Public Registry of Panama; present a detailed business plan, executed customer contracts, the Stripe/Paddle merchant IDs, and a recent revenue ledger; attach a notarized affidavit from the council certifying beneficial ownership and active commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or crypto-tainted source of funds such as anonymous digital asset transfers or high-volume micro-transactions typical of AIGC avatar subscriptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce 12 months of bank and PSP statements tied strictly to the foundation; provide a certified accountant's letter reconciling USD inflows from Stripe/Paddle to the SaaS dashboard; state in writing that no digital assets will cross the bank rails; if foundation capital was historically converted from bitcoin/ether, submit the regulated exchange's account statement showing a full fiat conversion chain and proof of origin before bank introduction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/AML screening hit triggered by founder, beneficial owner, or high-risk customer geography, particularly in AI avatar sectors with potential deepfake use-cases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a commercial OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening report for all UBOs; provide passport copies, proof of residence, and a source-of-wealth letter certified by a licensed attorney; attach a written compliance policy covering content moderation, identity-consent verification, watermarking, and a chargeback mitigation plan; if any end-user is based in a restricted jurisdiction, provide a Panamanian legal opinion confirming data-export and payment-processing compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient Panamanian economic substance, causing the bank's correspondent to suspect tax-evasion or shell risk in a jurisdiction previously on the FATF gray list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-empt with a Law 254 of 2021 economic substance file: a board resolution of the foundation council, the resident agent agreement, registered-office contract, and either (i) an exclusion analysis proving the foundation merely derives foreign-source passive license income without any relevant activity performed in Panama or (ii) evidence of local substance where relevant activities exist; attach the DGI/RUC registration and an updated Registro de Beneficiarios Finales filing certificate to demonstrate full transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry-wide underwriting concern over high chargeback/dispute ratios and refund abuse inherent to AI avatar video generation subscriptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a 6-month chargeback history report from Stripe/Paddle, simultaneously showing a chargeback ratio below 0.5%; include standard terms of service, refund policy, a data-protection notice, and evidence of the payment gateway's KYC verification layer; offer the bank a covenant limiting account activity to B2B licensing invoices where invoice numbers and customer names can be matched to the ledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a non-resident founder's capital injection into the PIF is a standard SWIFT MT103 sender's bank-to-beneficiary bank transfer of USD into a Tier 1 Panamanian account, with Field 70 instructions reading: 'CONTRIBUTION TO INSTITUTIONAL CAPITAL — PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION [NAME], FOUNDATION DEED NO. [X] OF [DATE], PUBLIC REGISTRY OF PANAMA, LAW 25/1995 — FOUNDER: [NAME]'. The bank will also require: an up-to-date Certificado de Personería Jurídica, the apostilled and notarized foundation deed and regulations (reglamento), the registered agent's letter confirming the foundation is in good standing, a passport copy of the founder, and a board resolution of the foundation council approving the capital injection and bank mandate. Where the injection exceeds USD 250,000, the bank may additionally request an audited source-of-funds statement or a notarized wealth affidavit. There are no Panamanian liquidity reserve, exchange control, or prior-approval requirements for the credits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Panama's dollarized economy permits unrestricted outbound clearing. International trade settlements should use SWIFT MT103 messages for the following: payments to cloud infrastructure and AI/GPU compute vendors, IP licensing royalties to foreign model providers, and salaries to non-resident contractors. For large one-off hardware acquisitions (GPU servers, storage), a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) available at sight through Banco General or Banistmo is permissible, though for SaaS software this rail is rarely necessary. Domestic clearing should be executed via the national ACH (Cámara de Compensación) for local payroll, Panamanian agent fees, and administrative expenses; high-value USD cheques and interbank settlements are processed by SBP-regulated clearing with no amount ceilings. All outbound MT103s must carry the precise beneficiary BIC, a valid Panamanian tax ID for local payroll payments, and the purpose code consistent with the ledger entry, such as 'PAYMENT FOR CLOUD COMPUTING SERVICES' or 'ROYALTY FOR AI MODEL LICENSE'. No central-bank permit or surrender obligation applies to any outbound disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) covering forecast subscription receivables disbursed by Stripe/Paddle from European exchanges
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and GBP/USD) to align long-dated commercial contracts with cloud-compute or licensing obligations
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on select Latin American currencies (BRL, COP, ARS, MXN) to hedge SaaS reseller payouts and regional customer refunds in the LatAm market
Vanilla European FX options (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) permitted strictly under a board-approved hedge policy, with no speculative positions
USD/PAB hedging instruments are unnecessary and unavailable given the Balboa's fixed 1:1 legal-tender peg to the US dollar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Anualidad de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a USD 30 administrative fine; failure to pay for three consecutive years may cause administrative strike-off of the foundation from the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Registry, Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within ninety (90) calendar days after the close of each fiscal year; or if fiscal year is calendar year, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Law 129 of 2020 range from USD 500 to USD 5,000 based on entity size and duration; repeated non-compliance can lead to suspension or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (via local licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; confirmed on each anniversary of the foundation's formation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a resident agent may result in cancellation of the foundation's registration and loss of legal capacity to transact in Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) — only if Panamanian-source income is derived
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 following the close of the calendar year; for fiscal-year taxpayers, within three months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% per month on unpaid taxes, up to 25%, plus statutory interest; persistent non-compliance may trigger administrative enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement for a passive Private Interest Foundation; audit is compelled if the foundation conducts commercial activity generating Panamanian-source gross annual income above the DGI threshold (currently USD 300,000) or is classified as a Gran Contribuyente (large taxpayer).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs is accepted for private foundations not in the public-interest scope; Panamanian local GAAP may apply to non-resident passive entities without Panamanian operations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama Private Interest Foundations must maintain a current beneficial owner register at the registered office and file an annual confirmation under Law 129 of 2020. A fresh confirmation is due within ninety (90) days after each fiscal year-end. Any change in the foundation's beneficiaries or council members that alters beneficial ownership must be reported to the DGI within fifteen (15) calendar days, and the annual filing is mandatory regardless of whether a shareholding transfer occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro de Miembros del Consejo de Fundación)
Minute Book of Council Resolutions (Libro de Actas del Consejo)
Register of Annual Franchise Tax Payment Receipts

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Passive PIF: USD 0 (no audit); if audit threshold is triggered: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) on net taxable income derived from Panamanian-source activities; a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with purely foreign-source revenue is outside the 25% charge by virtue of Panama's territorial tax system (Art. 694, Código Fiscal).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective tax on foreign-source income from AI avatar video SaaS subscriptions and licensing collected via Stripe/Paddle from non-resident customers; statutory micro-enterprise simplified regime at 2% of gross income for annual gross receipts up to B/.200,000; export-of-services regime treats services rendered to non-domiciled persons and used exclusively abroad as exempt or subject to a reduced 3% final rate; PIFs discharge their state contribution through the flat B/.300 (USD 300) annual foundation tax under Law 25 of 1995, Art. 63.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 700 (Declaración Jurada de Renta Anual) filed electronically through the tax administration portal of the Autoridad Nacional de Impuestos de Panamá (ANIP, successor of DGI) using the DTE electronic declaration system; the annual balance of the 25% CIT is paid together with the form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 700) by 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers; monthly advance tax payments of 1%-2% of gross income are due by the 15th day of the following month; the transfer pricing informative return is filed concurrently with Form 700.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within three months after the close of the fiscal year (31 March for taxpayers on a calendar-year basis); no extension is granted automatically, and interest accrues from the day following the statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Line 1a (Ingresos netos de fuente panameña)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from sales of AI avatar video generation software and related services where the economic use, delivery, or client exploitation occurs inside Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-sourced revenue. SaaS subscriptions collected through Stripe/Paddle from overseas customers, where the platform is delivered abroad and used outside Panama, are foreign-source and must be excluded; provide supporting subscriber and IP-geolocation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Line 1b (Ingresos de fuente extranjera o exenta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue economically sourced outside Panama or expressly exempted, including export services, foreign licensing royalties, and offshore AI processing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare foreign-source AI video generation and avatar licensing income in this section as informational items; these amounts remain outside the 25% charge but must be reconciled with transfer pricing documentation and the B/.300 annual foundation fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, operating expenses, salaries, depreciation, TP-adjustment deductions, and losses, including the 5-year NOL carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses traceable to Panama-source income; foreign overhead allocated to the PIF must follow arm's-length allocation and the OECD-aligned documentation; rental and staff costs shall be substantiated with invoices and payroll records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable base after deductions and loss carryforwards; result of Lines 1a minus Line 2, limited to Panama-source activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with no Panama-source income should show a nil taxable base; do not combine foreign-source SaaS collections with local deductions since our territorial regime taxes only the local branch ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculated at the 25% statutory rate applied to the Line 3a base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the base is nil, enter zero; if the simplified 2% regime was elected, compute 2% of gross Panama-source receipts instead of 25%; do not apply 25% to foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Lines 5a-5e (Retenciones, anticipos y saldo a pagar)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for withholding taxes suffered, monthly advance payments, and the resulting balance payable with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit 5% dividend WHT or 10% royalty WHT withheld by Panamanian payers; attach the TP report (Formulario 749) and confirm that the net amount is remitted from a Panamanian bank account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 700 attracts a surcharge and monthly resarcitorio interest of 1% on the unpaid tax, administrative fines of B/.500 to B/.10,000 per the Código Fiscal, and criminal exposure for false declarations; late payment carries an additional 10% non-deductible surcharge; the failure to file when no tax is due incurs a B/.250 administrative penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tasa Única Anual de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (B/.300 annual foundation tax) - single annual payment processed through the official bank collection network and acknowledged by ANIP/Registro Público; this is the PIF's principal state contribution when no Panama-source income is declared.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Payable every calendar year within the first quarter (1 January to 31 March); a foundation that fails to pay by 31 March incurs automatic interest and suspension of its legal standing and certificate of good standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foundation identification block (Nombres y apellidos del Consejo de la Fundación)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the PIF, registered number, registered agent (agente residente), tax ID (RUC-P or NIT), and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name and registration number from the Registro Público; appoint and maintain a licensed Panamanian registered agent and resident director to satisfy the law's minimum governance requirement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payment voucher - B/.300 annual tax (Art. 63, Law 25 of 1995)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Flat annual tax, not an income-based computation; applies to the existence of the foundation regardless of activity or revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign owner must ensure the registered agent funds the B/.300 annual payment from a Panamanian clearing account; the payment is not relieved by treaty and is the price of maintaining veil protection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment of the B/.300 annual foundation tax triggers accumulated interest at statutory rates, administrative fines, and the suspension or cancellation of the foundation's registration by the Registro Público; a cancelled PIF loses its separate legal personality and assets are exposed to attachment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% withholding tax on dividends distributed to shareholders or beneficiaries out of profits that were subject to the 25% corporate income tax in Panama; 10% withholding on distributions made out of untaxed Panama-source profits; distributions of foreign-source accumulated profits received by a PIF from its AI operating subsidiaries are not subject to Panamanian dividend WHT because the territorial regime treats them as foreign income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief on inbound dividends or royalties is invoked by a Panama PIF only in the source jurisdiction (e.g., OECD DTA partners such as Mexico, UAE, Korea, Singapore, Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, and Barbados) and requires: (i) a Certificate of Fiscal Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by ANIP; (ii) submission of the relevant DTA form and a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration to the foreign withholding agent; (iii) proof that the PIF is not a pass-through shell, including ESR documentation; and (iv) filing of a protective refund claim within the source jurisdiction's statutory window. Panama shelters the resulting foreign-source dividends from further domestic tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Panamanian payer for the use of software, algorithms, or AI video-generation IP in Panama are subject to a 10% statutory withholding tax; royalties received by a Panama PIF from a foreign licensee for use of the IP outside Panama are foreign-source and are not taxed or withheld in Panama. Interest paid by a Panamanian debtor to a non-resident lender is generally foreign-source and subject to 0% withholding, provided the lender is not acting through a Panamanian permanent establishment; intercompany interest remains subject to transfer pricing rules and the arm's-length principle.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.250,000 (USD 250,000) aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year: crossing this threshold triggers the mandatory preparation of the Local File (Estudio de Precios de Transferencia), the Master File, and the TP informative return (Formulario 749), which must be filed with the annual Form 700; penalties apply for failure to file or for inadequate documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Requirements (ESR), implemented through Decree 36 of 2021, apply to a PIF engaged in relevant activities, including holding business and IP exploitation: the foundation must demonstrate physical premises, qualified employees, and core income-generating activities in Panama, and must file the annual substance declaration with ANIP/Registro Público. A PIF holding AI avatar video-generation IP and deriving licensing royalties is treated as an IP-based relevant activity and carries a heightened burden to prove local decision-making, adequate staff, and active management of the IP; passive or 'pure holding' foundations enjoy a lighter substance test but must still maintain registered agent, records, and a Panamanian board of directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent income tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful under-declaration of Panama-source AI SaaS revenue, mischaracterization of domestic video-generation services as foreign-source income, fabrication of foreign clients, or use of nominee payment rails to hide taxable collections.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's Criminal Code and Ley 14 of 2016 impose imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for tax fraud, fines of up to three times the evaded tax, and mandatory restitution of the tax, statutory interest, and surcharges; the tax administration may also apply a 10% non-deductible surcharge and 1% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, the registered agent, and the beneficial owner who sign or cause false returns to be filed incur personal criminal liability, civil restitution of the evaded tax, asset freezes, travel bans (impedimento de salida), and disqualification from acting as directors in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham structure / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF as a shell that holds high-value AI/IP assets and collects licensing royalties without a Panamanian office, employees, board meetings, or business records; failure to file the ESR substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registro Público may impose ESR administrative fines, suspend or cancel the foundation's registration, and the tax authority may disregard the foundation as a sham for tax purposes, reattributing all revenue to the beneficial owner at the 25% corporate rate plus interest and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and protectors may be held jointly and severally liable for the foundation's unpaid taxes and third-party claims where the veil is pierced; aggravating conduct involving concealment of assets leads to civil restitution and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF to layer, conceal, or transfer proceeds derived from fraudulent AI subscription schemes, charge-back abuse, or unlicensed virtual-asset activity; failure to maintain beneficial-ownership records or to cooperate with the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 and Panama's Criminal Code impose imprisonment of 5 to 10 years for money laundering, increased to 10 to 15 years in aggravating circumstances, with fines up to B/.1,000,000 and forfeiture of funds held in Stripe/Paddle accounts or Panamanian bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council, the registered agent, and the beneficial owner are criminally liable as principals or accomplices; remedies include preventive travel bans, extradition, and personal seizure of assets beyond the foundation's patrimony.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file returns and to pay annual taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-filing of Form 700 by 31 March, non-payment of monthly advance income tax, non-submission of the TP return Formulario 749, or non-payment of the B/.300 annual foundation tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of B/.500 to B/.10,000, a 10% late-payment surcharge, monthly resarcitorio interest of 1%, and suspension or cancellation of the PIF's legal registration; interest and surcharges continue to accrue until full settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent are personally responsible for ensuring filing and payment; persistent non-compliance bars the use of the foundation's separate asset ring and subjects officers to civil liability for losses suffered by beneficiaries.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend withholding tax and distribution violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing Panama-source profits to the founder or beneficiaries without withholding the 5% dividend tax, or artificially classifying a distribution as a foreign-source capital gain or loan to avoid the withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is liable for the full under-withheld amount, a 50% penalty on the unpaid withholding, default interest at 1% monthly, and administrative fines; repeated violations are treated as tax fraud and escalate to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the foundation council who authorize a distribution without withholding are personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; where the distribution is disguised to conceal taxable profit, directors face criminal sanctions, travel bans, and civil restitution to the tax administration.
